tools.name: scan_website
tools.description: Run a measured health check of a public website homepage: speed (server response, page weight, scripts, image formats), security (HTTPS, certificate expiry, security headers), domain registration expiry, email authentication (MX, SPF, DMARC), search basics (title, description, headings, indexability

tools.name: check_ai_search_readiness
tools.description: Check whether AI assistants and answer engines can read and quote a public website: which AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others) its robots.txt allows or blocks, whether it publishes llms.txt, which structured data types it declares, how its title and description

tools.name: score_local_presence
tools.description: Score a local business on three pillars, website (45 percent), Google reviews (30 percent) and Google Business Profile (25 percent), and return an overall 0 to 100 score, a letter grade, each pillar with its verdict, and the top fixes. tools.name: explain_check
tools.description: Explain one Site Check check by its id (as returned by scan_website): what it measures, the pass and fail thresholds, why it matters, how to fix it, and the typical effort. Static reference, no network access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "site-check" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: scan_website · Private data: scan_website · Public sink: scan_website · Destructive: scan_website.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: scan_website · Private data: scan_website · Public sink: scan_website · Destructive: scan_website

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
